wiki/surnames/Miagostovic.content:
Miagostović
Bearers

q. paron Ivan Miagostović — d. before 1651-03-09; ship “Sveti Ivan Krstitelj”; estate represented by donna Caterina sua relitta, sons Mihovil (Michiel), Grgur (Gregorio), Šimun (Simon) (doc. 55).

wiki/surnames/Miani.title: Miani
wiki/surnames/Miani.content:
Miani
Venetian patrician house.
Bearers

Anzolo Miani — Venetian senator, signatory of doc 22 (1684) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Midda.title: Midda
wiki/surnames/Midda.content:
Midda
Bearers

maggior Midda — maggiore (military rank) in Zadar 1686; his properties bordered (da maistro le ragioni del signor maggior Midda) the San Simeone-parish house purchased by Stojan Janković (doc 143, footnote citing the 24 July 1684 instrument) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Mihaljevic.title: Mihaljevic
wiki/surnames/Mihaljevic.content:
Mihaljević / Miljević / Miličević
Drniški origin family of harambaše. Spelt Mihaglievich in Italian.
Bearers

Matija (Mattio) Mihaljević da Drniš, habitante nel borgo della Marina (Šibenik) — 1648-08-01 deposes about the Battle of Zečevo and Vuk Mandušić’s death (doc. 43 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).
Mihail Miličević rečeni Kovač — 1663-06-22 named paga intera di soldato in Makarska, “intervenuto fra gli altri nel fatto suddetto” of killing the famous Turk Alija Bojičić of Zadvarje (doc. 132). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
Smoljan Smiglianich (alias Mihalevich) — see Smoljan Smiljanić — 1656 lawsuit names him “Smoglian Smiglianich o Mihalevich” (doc. 103). His paternal patronymic was Mihaljević; the more famous Smiljanić surname comes from his maternal kin.

wiki/surnames/Mihatovic.title: Mihatovic
wiki/surnames/Mihatovic.content:
Mihatović
Bearers in Desnica II

harambaša Giozich Mihatović (Jošić Mihatović) — Blato 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Possibly same as Đošić (Jošić).

wiki/surnames/Mihelic.title: Mihelic
wiki/surnames/Mihelic.content:
Mihelić
Single attestation: conte Jakov (Giacomo) Mihelić — 1647-12-17 — “conte di conti di tutte le ville de cristiani di Campo Piero, che sono il numero di tredici” — knez nad knezovima of the 13 Christian villages of Petropolje (doc. 18).

wiki/surnames/Mikovic.title: Mikovic
wiki/surnames/Mikovic.content:
Miković
Single attestation: harambaša Smoljan Miković — 1648-07-17: “Uskoci iz Đevrsaka naseljeni kod Petrčana od 50 ljudi izgubili dvojicu” at Ribnik (doc. 39 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).
(Note: a Smoljan Đerverščović da Đevrske / Smoglian Geverscovich in doc. 70 — 1653 — is a different cognate-form referring to the same village/cluster but used as a Đevrske-derived demonym, not a parallel Miković. See Đerverščović.)

wiki/surnames/Milatovic.title: Milatovic
wiki/surnames/Milatovic.content:
Milatović
Single attestation: Martin Milatović — 1679-05-16, in Valier’s prison in Zadar accused of selling Milovan Garković (son of Radojica) to Turks (doc. 247).

nipote (nephew): also called Martin (Milatović).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Martin Milatović — accused raider in 1693-11-04 raid on Gorica (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Possibly the same man as the 1679 attestation.

wiki/surnames/Milic.title: Milic
wiki/surnames/Milic.content:
Milić
Single attestation: harambaša Martin Milić — 1648-07-17: “Uskoci iz Popovića naseljeni kod Nina od 54 čovjeka izgubili dva” at Ribnik (doc. 39 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).

wiki/surnames/Miljanic.title: Miljanic
wiki/surnames/Miljanic.content:
Miljanić
Two distinct geographic Miljanić-clusters appear: Gračac (the senior 1647 cluster) and Čučulovci → Vrsi (the post-1648 settlement).
Bearers

Žure (Giure) Miljanić — 1647-08-16 led the Grazac raid as guide (doc. 15 — Petar Smiljanić’s deposition). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
Vido Miljanić — brother of Žure; came from Grazac after the raid as Turkish negotiator for ransoms (doc. 15).
harambaša Petar Miljanić — 1648-07-17: “Uskoci iz Čučulovaca naseljeni u Vrsima od 70 pješaka poginulo šest” at Ribnik (doc. 39).
Mattio Miglianich da Cuculovaz — 1653-01-16 co-signs the proxy authorising Smiljanić to plead in Venice (doc. 70).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Multiple Miljanić bearers in 1696 Obrovac inhabitant list (doc. 284) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II:

Giadrijem Miljanić (Jadrijem Miglianich) — Obrovac 1696.
Mattio Miljanić (Mate Miljanić) — Obrovac 1696. (Possibly same as 1653 da Cuculovaz.)
Stipan Miljanić — Obrovac 1696.
Bože (Boso) Miljanić — Obrovac 1696.
Nikola Miljanić — Obrovac 1696.
Mattio Miljanić (Mattio Miglianich) — captain of Krušev (Crussevo); 1704 rebel leader in Bukovica revolt (doc. 352) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

The Miljanić Obrovac group is one of those families noted by Desnica’s footnote as still living in Kruševo, the village adjacent to Obrovac (continuity to modern times) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Milkovic.title: Milkovic
wiki/surnames/Milkovic.content:
Milković
Bunjevac starešina family from Medviđa Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre (Šarić identifies the Milkovići as a Bunjevac starešina family).
Bearers

Mate Milković of Kruševo near Obrovac — 1554, debtor of a Šibenik butcher (Šarić citation).
harambaša Ilija Milković — second-in-command in Mitrović’s Žegar circle. 1648-07-29 deposes about Sorić’s Udbina raid (doc. 32). 1654-07-01 promoted to cavalleria leggera by Dolfin for blowing up Zvonigrad (doc. 80). 1656-03-04 assigned to guard the Krka passes (doc. 101). 1658-06-28 named alongside Janko in Bernardo’s concerto with Petar Zrinski (doc. 106). 1659-02-11 wounded with Janko at Cetina (doc. 112). 1659-03-01 — died in Zadar; buried Sv. Domenico (docs. 114, 115).
Marco Milković — 1661-03-01 named (with Petar Grgurica) capi de Morlacchi by Andrea Korner (doc. 118). 1663-11-21 — died bravamente combattendo (doc. 135). 1664-05-21 succeeded by Matia Mirković.
Šimun Milković — 1668-09-21 supplica to Doge: of his 12 uskočio family men, 10 perished, he and brother Mihail are slaves; supplicates ransom (doc. 160).
Mihail Milković — Šimun’s brother, slave in Turkey 1668.
harambaša Šimun Milković — 1672-02-05 originally promised Bokanjac as settlement site for 25 families of Ivosevci + 11 of Butoraz (doc. 200). The Parčići dispute the assignment.
kapetan Šimun Milković — 1671-12-17 settles in Dračevac with brother and son (doc. 199; “fratello et nipote — no. 3”).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Bože Milković (Boze Milcovich) — serdar of Lower Kotari by 1691; previously already governor; brother killed by Ilija Janković’s followers 1692; led 2,000 men to Malpaga; reconciled with Zaviša Mitrović 1692 by Dolfin’s mediation; partook in Liga 1696; led mission of Filip Jakić & Stankovic to expose Žegar raid 1693 (docs. 224, 236, 243, 247, 268, 286). 1699 supplied 25 sessane and 8 horses for Grimani; testified in Sfakioto’s protocols (docs. 314, 316, 319). Bedridden ill Dec 1699 (doc. 323); died ~1700, succeeded by Lazar Smiljanić as serdar of Lower Kotari Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Bože Milković’s “barba” (uncle) — anonymous; destroyed Zvonigrad in past war (“fu ravinato nella guerra passata da mio barba”) per Bože’s 1699 testimony (doc. 316) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
harambaša Mede Milcović (Mede Milicovich) — see Krmpotić entry; settled Bukovica Krmpote and Parčić, granted Medvidja fields 1693 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs. 263, 301).

wiki/surnames/Milohanic.title: Milohanic
wiki/surnames/Milohanic.content:
Milohanić (Milokanić)
Catholic Vlach kindred with branches on both sides of the Habsburg-Ottoman border Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Likely linked to medieval Milohanić village near Korlat (Banadego). Nikola-Milokanic-b1521 — Istria-born former Muslim (“Osman”), testified 1591 about ~50-year cycle Istria → Ottoman → Istria with 184 kin. Grgur-Milohanovic-b????-Nova-Vas founded Miljacki (Zemunik Gornji) 1561, retreated 1570 with 40 families to Žbandalj near Poreč.
Bearers in this wiki

Nikola-Milokanic-b1521 — testified 1591, born Istria, lived Banpolje (Lika) under Ottomans
Grgur-Milohanovic-b????-Nova-Vas — village founder (1561)

wiki/surnames/Milovanic.title: Milovanic
wiki/surnames/Milovanic.content:
Milovanić
Vlach kindred. Petar-Milovanic-b????-Medvidja attested 1518 as catonarius districtus Zelengradi — earliest dated record. By 1528 head of Bukovica dzemat in Medviđa Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Defected to Venice 1538; entered Venetian military service. 1570 captain Slade Milovanić commanded Croatian cavalry on Zadar territory.
Bearers in this wiki

Petar-Milovanic-b????-Medvidja — knez, head of Bukovica dzemat (1518/1528)
Tomas-Milovanic-b????-Medvidja — knez, brother of Petar
Slade-Milovanic-b???? — kapetan of Croat cavalry (1570)

wiki/surnames/Milovic.title: Milovic
wiki/surnames/Milovic.content:
Milović
Bearers

harambassa Migliovich — 1648-08-01 with Smiljanić at Sezevo (doc. 43).
Ilia Milovich — 1653-01-16 co-signs Smiljanić proxy (doc. 70).
Ilia da Radassinovzi (knez) — 1683-11 in fra Grga Šutić’s report from Vrana (doc. 333). Possibly a Radošinovac sub-line.

wiki/surnames/Mircetic.title: Mircetic
wiki/surnames/Mircetic.content:
Mirčetić
Bearers

Frane (Francesco) Mirčetić — 1684-01-04 leads 400 households of Zagorje Morlachi to settle in Vrana; counterpart of Matija Nakić (doc. 362). Brings them in with all family destroyed houses behind them.
Rade Mirčetić — capo de Morlacchi 1684-02-22 (doc. 377) — among Frane’s lieutenants.
Radovan Mitrichievich da Budin — 1680-05-10 named as one of the six Morlachi who kidnapped Alil & Camera near Gračac (doc. 266); spelling variant of Mirčetić.

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Frane Mirčetić — continues to appear as harambaša of Vrana; signatory of the 1684 Vrana petitions to Mocenigo (docs 35, 36) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Mirkovic.title: Mirkovic
wiki/surnames/Mirkovic.content:
Mirković
Bearers

Matija Mirković da Kožulovo polje — 1653-01-16 co-signs proxy (doc. 70).
harambaša Matija Mirković — 1663-05-08 leader at the Nadin pass with men of Kosulovac, Bukovica-Bukničani, Frletići and Diklo (doc. 130).
kapetan Matija Mirković — 1664-05-21 named serdar by Contarini in place of the killed Marko Milković (doc. 137). One of Contarini’s two pre-1664 serdari (the other being Kiakić).
Rade Mirčetić — 1683-12-26 with pop Lazar Dragović in the 1500-family Zagorje plea (doc. 358); same as Frane Mirčetić — see Mircetic.
Mirko Knežević — 1663-05-08 sudac of Posedarje (doc. 131); kin link to Mirković unclear.
Pavissa Ivančević and Frane Mirčetić — 1684-01-04 are described together as the Zagorje uskakanje leaders (docs. 362, 363).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Aurelio Mirković (Aurelio Mircovich) — difensor of Pago; signer of Pago salt contract 1694 (doc. 279) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Mistakieli.title: Mistakieli
wiki/surnames/Mistakieli.content:
Mistakieli
Single attestation: dottor Nicolò Mistakieli — 1656-06-15 medic in Zadar, sued Smoljan Smiljanić for treatment fees (43 reali) for repeatedly tending the wounds of Smoljan’s uncles Ilija and Filip Smiljanić (doc. 103). Probably Greek-of-Latin-rite Zadar surname.

wiki/surnames/Mitrovic.title: Mitrovic
wiki/surnames/Mitrovic.content:
Mitrović (later Janković-Mitrović)
The clan that would become the legendary kotarska lineage Janković-Mitrović. Per Stojan Janković’s 1670 supplica (doc. 170, Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I), five brothers — Janko, Giovanni, Stefan, Pavle and Andrija — abandoned their patria of Žegar at the start of the Candian War (~1646–47) and brought ~70 households / ~150 fighting men into Venetian Ravni Kotari, settling at Posedarje.
The change of family-name from Mitrović (the patronymic from grandfather q. Dimitri) to Janković (from Janko, the eldest brother) happens in Venetian usage during Janko’s own lifetime; the official pay-rolls and documents continue to call them Mitrovich into the 1680s.
Bearers attested in this source

Janko Mitrović q. Dimitri — Žegar → Posedarje; harambaša → serdar; d. 1659-02-28 in Zadar.
Vukadin Mitrović (probably brother or cousin of Janko) — Žegar; harambaša; d. 1653 defending Novigrad.
Jakov Mitrović, son of Vukadin — slave at one point; pay assigned to him 1653 (doc. 74) and again 1681-05-08 by ducal of Doge A. Contarini for unpaid biscotto arrears (doc. 274).
Giacomo Mitrović da Islam — captured by Stojan Janković (doc. 187, 1671 plundering of Greek merchants in Posedarje); separately Giacomo Mitrović bandit of Posedarje pardoned 1673 (doc. 204).
Stojan Janković (= Stojan Mitrović) — son of Janko; the famous kavalier.
Sabba Janković — son of Janko; m. Maria Lase 1676-08-17.
Ilija Mitrović (the bandit) — son of Janko; banished 1680; instigator of the Vrana uprising 1683–84.
Konstantin Janković — son of Stojan; capitan of 50 fanti from 1679-02-09.
Zorzi-Alvise Janković b. 1674-04-23, son of Stojan and Vinka.
Anastazija Janković b. 1675-02-26, daughter of Stojan and Vinka.
Josip Janković b. 1677-09-30, son of Stojan and Antonia Reci.
Nikola Janković — son of Stojan, in cavalry from 1675.
Janja Janković (b. ~1655 d. 1680) — daughter of Janko; m. Dimitri Nikolić-Pivljanin.
Mitar/Dimitri Mitrović “da Grazaz” — slave of Stojan in his Zadar house, escaped 1680 (doc. 266, 267).
Alil son of Mitar Mitrović da Grazaz — captured slave (10 May 1680, doc. 266).

Notes

The kin-link Mitrović ↔ Pivljanin (through Janja’s marriage) is essential context for the 1683–84 Vrana uprising: Bajo Nikolić-Pivljanin and his brother Mitar shared this family.
The Sinobad case (April 1684, docs. 391, 396) accuses Ilija Mitrović of murdering Perica Sinobad (Jovan’s father) and burning his houses in Budin.

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
The Mitrović/Janković lineage is the central thread of Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II from 1684 through 1731, with extensive documentation of the second and third generations.
Second generation (children of Janko)

Stojan Janković — repeatedly referenced as “quondam kavalier Gianco” by 1689 onwards; the 1689 Cornaro attestation for his brother Zaviša notes Stojan’s earlier service Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 225).
Zaviša/Sabba Janković (Saviša Mitrović detto Janco) — central figure of the chunk; Cornaro’s 1689 attestation documents his deeds at Sinj, Zadar, Vrcerev Vakup (where wounded), and Knin Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 225). 1692-08-20 partnership contract with Bortolo and Zuanne Gambiraži of Obrovac for 1000 ducats trading capital, brokered by Lomazzi (doc. 254). 1692-03-17 surety bond of 2000 ducats with Oratio Lantana for behavior of brother Ilija (doc. 246). Pay raised from 30 to 50 ducats/month by Doge Silvestro Valier dukal of 1697 (docs. 303, 306). 1696-06-27 made cavalier of San Marco by Doge Valier (doc. 288). 1701-06-05 took oath at relics of St. Šimun in Zadar challenged by conte Frane Posedarski (doc. 330). 1701-11-26 bought half of Olib island from conte Giacomo Califfi q. Francesco for 8000 ducats (doc. 336). 1702 led troops to Italy in War of Spanish Succession; died early 1702 leaving widow + 3 creatures including son Ilija. Pay raised to 50 ducats. Could not write Italian — Tomadelli signed for him (doc. 279); signed in Cyrillic (“Ja Zaviša Mitrović potrugjem”, doc. 270). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Ilija Mitrović (the rebellious) — central villain 1690–1693; refused to meet provveditor Molin 1690 (doc. 228); fled Obrovac on Molin’s arrival; killed Bože Milković’s brother and other Morlachs (doc. 243); reconciled with Milković and Sinobad parties by Dolfin’s mediation 1692 (doc. 247); 15 ducats/month restored by terminacija of 1 April 1692 (doc. 248); accused of murdering Andrea Tomišić in Gorica 1692 (doc. 268); died of natural causes (“rilasciata natura”) late 1693 (doc. 269); per docs. 305, 379 he was the third brother of Stojan and Zaviša, lived in Zadar with wife and children. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Third generation (children of Stojan, Zaviša, Ilija)

Konstantin Janković — son of Stojan; capitano of Croat cavalry from 1686 (ducal 7 Nov 1686, no public expense); died 1692-02-27 aged ~12; buried in Greek church of Sant’Elia by curato don Andrea Caldana. Death recorded by Caldana (doc. 244). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Nikola Janković — son of Stojan; raised 500 oltramarini per ducal 7 Nov 1686 (doc. 249).
Mijat (Michiel) Janković — son of Ilija; died 1692-08-23; buried at Sant’Elia (doc. 255).
Nicolò Mitrović — son of Ilija; appointed capitano of Croat cavalry company (formerly Konstantin’s) on 1692-04-01, with tenente training troops until of age (doc. 249); ducal of 21 Sept 1702 confirmed life tenure (doc. 369); died 1709, replaced by brother Stojan (younger).
Stojan Mitrović (younger) — son of Ilija (the rebellious), nephew of original kavalier Stojan; made captain of new 50-man company guarding Keglević fort 1701 (doc. 325); given Šimun Jere’s cavalry company by Carlo Pisani in 1712/13 (doc. 371); 1709 inherited brother Nicolò’s cavalry company.
Marija Mitrović — daughter of Ilija the rebellious; married Vučen Stojisavljević of Vrlika; mother of Petar Mitrović-Stojisavljević raised in the Mitrović household (doc. 379).
Ilija Janković (younger) — son of Zaviša; minor at father’s death 1702; reserved 50 ducats then 20; 1701 captain of Italy-bound company; 1705-08-20 granted hereditary count title with Nicolò and Stojan (doc. 360); 1717 made full serdar of Upper Kotari (40 ducats/month); died ~1731. Possibly party to alleged duel with priest Marko Mesić at Lukovo (doc. 364, footnote). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Fourth generation

Kirijak Dedić-Mitrović (Janković) — sister’s son of deceased serdar Ilija Janković (the younger); alfiere; appointed serdar of Upper Kotari 1731-11-01 by Vendramin (docs. 381–384); minor at appointment, deputy assigned. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Other Mitrović bearers

Filippo Mitrović — capitano of 56-foot company in Obrovac, dismissed by Molin Jan 1690 (doc. 227). Distinct from Filip Smiljanić. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Rade Mitrović — Obrovac inhabitant 1696 (doc. 284). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Petar Mitrović (= Petar Stojisavljević) — assumed Mitrović cognomen having been raised in the Mitrović house; appointed serdar of Knin Krajina 1726-02-23 by Niccolò Erizzo (docs. 376, 379); removed by ducal of 1 Dec 1729 in favor of Giacomo Sinobad (doc. 380). See Stojisavljevic. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

1705 hereditary count title
Doge Alvise Mocenigo dukal of 1705-08-20 granted hereditary conte title to Ilija (younger), Nicolò, and Stojan Janković-Mitrović in recognition of family service Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 360).
Notes

Doc. 288 ducal confounds “carambassà Gianco Mitrouich capo principale de Morlachi di Obrouazzo” with “sardar Stojan Mitrovich detto Gianco” — these are two distinct persons (Janko = founder; Stojan = Janko’s son called Gianco).
The 1670 Janković investitura on the house of Jusuf-aga Tunić at Islam continued to be referenced as a Mitrović holding in 1700 with 400 gognali (docs. 329, 330).

wiki/surnames/Mivcanica.title: Mivcanica
wiki/surnames/Mivcanica.content:
Mivčanica
Pejan-Mivcanica-b????-Podgorje was a primićur recorded in the 1530 sumarni defter Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Pejan-Mivcanica-b????-Podgorje — primićur (1530)

wiki/surnames/Mocenigo.title: Mocenigo
wiki/surnames/Mocenigo.content:
Mocenigo
Venetian patrician house. Bearers in this source served as provveditor general and doge.
Bearers

Domenico Mocenigo — Provveditor General estraordinario dell’armi in Dalmazia et Albania, arrived May 1684; main correspondent docs 1–43; eventual scapegoat for Sinj defeat April 1685 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Alvise Mocenigo II — doge from 1700; signs ducali on Dalmatian affairs through volume’s later docs Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

In Desnica II (1684–1749) — extended

Mocenigo (the predecessor provveditor) — 1684-07-15 terminacija granted Ilija Mitrović 15 ducats/month (doc. 248) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Aluise (Alvise) Mocenigo — provveditor generale of Dalmatia late 1696–1702, succeeding Daniel Dolfin; ordered Resep Budisalić’s release Jan 1697 (docs. 300, 301); later Doge; dukal 1705-08-20 granted hereditary count title to Ilija, Nicolò, Stojan Mitrović-Janković (doc. 360); dukal of 22 March 1702 (doc. 342) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Cà Mocenigo — Venetian residence in Venice; 1704 lodging of Franciscan Pavlo Vušković where Mattio Žabetić was seen during the Bukovica revolt aftermath (doc. 357) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Modre.title: Modre
wiki/surnames/Modre.content:
Modre
The “Turco Modre” gave his name to Modrino selo village near St. Peter’s church in Bukovica, his casale assigned to Jovan Sinobad 1692 (doc. 259) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Described as congiunto (relative) of Sinobad — implying the family had Christian and Muslim branches separated by religion. The casale dispute with Radoš and Sava Kresović continued into 1697.
Notes

Likely a personal name/byname rather than a heritable surname; preserved in the toponym Modrino selo.

wiki/surnames/Molin.title: Molin
wiki/surnames/Molin.content:
Molin
Venetian patrician.
Bearers in Desnica II

Alessandro Molin (Aleksandar Molino) — provveditor generale in Dalmatia 1689–1692; established Obrovac salt scale; appointed Casanova governor of Obrovac; divided Kotari into upper/lower; appointed serdars Zaviša Mitrović (Upper) and Bože Milković (Lower); appointed Sinobad governor of Knin; etc. (docs. 226–242, 257) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Succeeded by Daniel Dolfin Feb 1692.

wiki/surnames/Morosini.title: Morosini
wiki/surnames/Morosini.content:
Morosini
Venetian patrician (Doge).
Bearers in Desnica II

Francesco Morosini — Doge of Venice; ducale of 1690-05-21 awarding 10 ducats/month to capt. Marko Smiljanić (doc. 233); ducale of 1692-10-22 confirming Lomazzi as Illyrian interpreter (doc. 257) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Movicuna.title: Movicuna
wiki/surnames/Movicuna.content:
Močivuna
Morlach lineage that uskočio from Ottoman village Jakorševci “molti anni” before 1669 (Priuli’s terminacija doc. 167) and settled in Bokanjac above Zadar (Spianata). Multi-generational pravoslavni line — christened at Sv. Ilija Zadar.
Bearers

Vuk (Vučko) Močivuna — d. 1666-05-01 at Zečevo (doc. 151, glagolska zabeleška from Filipjakov: “poginu dobri junak Vučko Močivuna” — in a battle in which 73 Kotarane were killed). Pay 4 ducati/month assigned 1653-10-22 by Dolfin (doc. 76 — “di statura bassa, giovane sbarbato d’ anni vinti due in circa” → b. ~1631) for beheading a Turk and presenting the head to the provveditore. Earlier 1650-09-20 same pay, transferred 1666-05-21 to brother Vučen (doc. 155).
Vučen Močivuna — brother of Vuk; 4 ducati/month inherited 1666-05-21. Distinct from a Vučin Močivuna who held two Turkish slaves (Vuk Cusat and Vido Pagin) on the Spianata 1665 (doc. 146).
Vučko Močivuna — likely the same as Vuk; harambaša 1662-04-12 (doc. 125) — Korner forbids him assembling raids without written permission.
Milisav (Milissa, Milosav) Močivuna — uskočio “many years before” 1669 from Jakorševci (doc. 167); harambaša; pay 4 ducati + peso di biscotto/month from 1669-10-10 by Priuli. Wife Kata baptised slave-girl Maria 1677-01-07 at Sv. Ilija (doc. 231). Son Matija (Matio) baptised 1663-07-12 stile vecchio (doc. 134); compare Sapissa Giancovichia and comare Anizza Murlaca. With Smoljan Đevrsković and Luka Kožulović 1671-06-21 represented the pravoslavni Morlaci against the Trećoredci re Sv. Ivan church in Spianata (doc. 193). Bokanjac capitan 1684-03-01 (doc. 381).
Todor Močivuna — d. in Cetina (the 1666 conflict); widow Anica relicta (doc. 164, 1668-12-23). Children: son Dragoslav + 3 daughters in pupillar età. Anica granted 1 peso di biscotto/month for support of children (doc. 164).
Anica (Anizza) udovica Toda Močivune — 1668; possibly the same as the comare Anizza Murlaca at the 1663 baptism of Mate (doc. 134).
Dragoslav Močivuna — son of Todor (1668).

wiki/surnames/Municasa.title: Municasa
wiki/surnames/Municasa.content:
Municasa
Bearers

major Municasa — major of corazze (heavy cuirassier cavalry) Feb 1685 (doc 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Murgic.title: Murgic
wiki/surnames/Murgic.content:
Murgić
Lika surname (not necessarily Bunjevac itself). Foremost member: Ivan-Murgic-b????-Perusic († 1881) — career officer in the Vojna krajina, whose posthumous Vienac article (1882) is the last izvorna svjedočanstva of self-identifying Bunjevci in Lika–Primorje Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Erdeljanović 1930 mistakenly assumed Murgić was Bunjevac (Šarić corrects this).

wiki/surnames/Muskovic.title: Muskovic
wiki/surnames/Muskovic.content:
Mušković
Old Vlach kindred — territorialized katun at Muskovci near Obrovac (catunar Dien Mušković, 1433 Lika kraljevski Vlasi charter) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1544: 25 families fled Lika summer pasture across to Habsburg, settled at Prilisce under Nikola-Zrinski-b???? as hereditary libertini. Catholic, čakavski-ikavski.

wiki/surnames/Najcinovic.title: Najcinovic
wiki/surnames/Najcinovic.content:
Najčinović (Jančić)
Vlach kindred attested in Benković nahija from 1528. Surname forms appear interchangeably (“Petar Jančić” in 1528–30 register = “Petar Najčinović” in later sources) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. After 1538 defection: kapetan in Podnovje (novigradski distrikt); some moved to Venetian Istria (Dvigrad, Labinština).
Bearers in this wiki

Petar-Najcinovic-b????-Dobruca-Vas — knez, head of Benković dzemat
Pavel-Najcinovic-b???? — brother of Petar
Nenad-Jancic-b????-Dobruca-Vas — relative
Pavel-Jancic-b????-Glucje, Radul-Jancic-b????-Glucje, Juraj-Jancic-b????-Glucje — relatives in Glučje (Karin)
Milic-Jancic-b????-Kucista, Mihovil-Jancic-b????-Kucista, Biljan-Jancic-b????-Kucista, Martin-Jancic-b????-Kucista — Kućišta (Zrmanja)

wiki/surnames/Najerlovic.title: Najerlovic
wiki/surnames/Najerlovic.content:
Najerlović
Bearers

Radko (Radivoj) Najerlović — conte of Vrana; signatory of the 1684 Vrana petitions to Mocenigo (docs 35, 36) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Nakic.title: Nakic
wiki/surnames/Nakic.content:
Nakić
Bearers

harambaša Matija Nakić — 1683-12-09 with the Petropolje conti pleads via fra Petar Tintić for protection (doc. 349). 1684-01-04 with Frane Mirčetić petitions for uskakanje of 1000+ households (doc. 362). 1684-01-05 Donà gives him a panno-suit and 2 cechini (doc. 363). Sent to Venice; awaited at Šibenik with hostages 1684-03-14 (doc. 382).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

karambaša Nakić — leader of 500 Trogir-territory Morlaks; July 1684 mentioned in dispatches (docs 17, 18); at the Sinj defeat April 1685 he gave his own horse to the wounded provveditor Marin Michiel, saving him (doc 61); January 1686 reports the Bosnian Pasha’s march from Banja Luka toward Livno (doc 125); November 1686 sent by Stojan Janković with Vuconie Cvitanović to warn the Zadar contado of the Turkish irruption (doc 155) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Nanic.title: Nanic
wiki/surnames/Nanic.content:
Nanić
Bukovica surname attested in Žegar.
Bearers attested

Ilija Nanić of Žegar — co-leader of the 1704 Bukovica revolt alongside pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža and Mattio Žabetić.

Notes

Per Desnica’s 1951 editorial footnote, the Nanić surname is still present in Žegar today (1951). Together with Zelić, Radmilović, and Vukčević, the families “came in 1648 with the Jankovićs to Budim near Posedarje and during the Morean War many returned to Lika; Budim is today (1951) ruins” (footnote to doc 115). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

In Desnica II (1684–1749) — extended

Ilija Nanić “da Xegar/Segar” — captain of Islam and Kašić 1698 (doc. 309); 1702 named arbitrator by Brgud villagers in Lisičić-Brgud dispute (doc. 348); one of three ringleaders of the 1704 Bukovica revolt alongside pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža and Mattio Žabetić (docs. 352, 356, 357); banished, condemned to death in absentia, fled to Lika (Imperial side) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Negri.title: Negri
wiki/surnames/Negri.content:
Negri
Bearers in Desnica II

Marin Angelo de Negri (Marin Negri) — segretario of the Doge; signed several dukals 1697–1702 (docs. 306, 345, 347) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Nenadic.title: Nenadic
wiki/surnames/Nenadic.content:
Nenadić
Poljica family. 1506: Ivanis-Nenadic-b????-Poljica (brother of the then Mostar voivod) fled to Ottoman territory at Ottoman invitation Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Ivanis-Nenadic-b????-Poljica — defected 1506

wiki/surnames/Nizic.title: Nizic
wiki/surnames/Nizic.content:
Nižić
Single attestation: don Šimun (Simon) Nižić — 1647-04-01 sent by Foscolo to the Velebit Podgorje to persuade Morlachi to uskočiti (doc. 3). The accompanying note mentions “li 4 moscettoni che gia feci pretar al quondam Nisich” (doc. 7) — a relative previously deceased.

wiki/surnames/Nuncovic.title: Nuncovic
wiki/surnames/Nuncovic.content:
Nuncović
Bearers

Nuncović — Venetian confidente (informant); July 1685 wrote letters from Ottoman territory to governator Marinović of Forte Opus reporting the Bosnian Pasha’s preparations against Duare (Zadvarje) (doc 82, line 3903) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Oluic.title: Oluic
wiki/surnames/Oluic.content:
Oluić
Bearers

Vučić Oluić — Morlach newcomer settled at Bilišane above Obrovac; in late January 1686 reported to Stojan Janković that the Croatian ban had crossed into Bosnia four days earlier with great damage; Oluić’s partita had been at Sinogora (= Siva Gora / Sitna Gora?) between Lika and Krbava and had seen the smoke (doc 123, 28 Jan 1686 deposition of Stojan) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Omeljic.title: Omeljic
wiki/surnames/Omeljic.content:
Omeljić
Bearers

wiki/surnames/Pivljanin-Nikolic.title: Pivljanin-Nikolic
wiki/surnames/Pivljanin-Nikolic.content:
Nikolić-Pivljanin
Hajduk family from Piva (Plav region), resident in Zadar from end of the Candian War to start of the Morean War (Desnica’s footnote on doc. 211). Brothers’ names: Bajo, Mitar/Dmitar, Petar.
The family’s link to the Mitrović-Janković of Žegar is established by Mitar’s marriage to Janja Janković (sister of Stojan), 1675-01-17 at Sv. Ilija Zadar (doc. 210). Their son Nikola Nikolić was baptised 1677-10-01 (doc. 236).
Bearers

Bajo Nikolić-Pivljanin — the celebrated hajduk; in this corpus 1675–1684 lives in Zadar as paid cavalryman of capt. Soliman’s company. 1675-04-26 offers to take in the Turkish slave Omer Mustafa (doc. 138 — wait, that’s a different transaction). 1680-05-03 leasing the prado in Sovare at Suhovare from Turks (doc. 265). 1682-06-02 Korner orders him not to abuse his brother Petar (doc. 284). Joins his nephew/brother-in-law Ilija Mitrović in the Vrana uprising 1683; pardoned by Donà 1683-12-08 (doc. 347). Reassigned to Kotor 1684-04-12 with brother Mitar (doc. 393).
Mitar (Dmitar/Dimitri) Nikolić-Pivljanin — Bajo’s brother. Married Janja Janković 1675-01-17 (doc. 210). Son Nikola Nikolić b. 1677-10-01 at Sv. Ilija (doc. 236). Goes AWOL Jan 1684; pardoned 1684-02-19 (doc. 376). Per Desnica’s footnote on doc. 376: “Mitar Nikolić, brat Baja Pivljanina, boravio je, kao i ovaj, u Zadru, kao plaćeni vojnik mletačke konjice” — and joined Ilija Mitrović’s rebellion (Mitar was married to Ilija’s sister, that is, was Stojan and Ilija’s zet).
Petar Nikolić — 1682-06-02 Korner forbids Bajo to abuse him (doc. 284).
Nikola Nikolić — son of Mitar and Janja, b. 1677-10-01.
Simeon Nikolić-Pivljanin — son of Bajo and his wife Manda, baptismal record (doc. 226 head — birth attestation in the Sv. Ilija registers).

Notes

The 1685 attestation by Bajo “havendo già 7 anni in Zadar” implicit places him in Zadar from c. 1671. (Desnica’s footnote on doc. 211 puts the Pivljanini in Zadar from “od svršetka kandijskog pa do početka morejskog rata” — i.e. 1669–1684.)

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Bajo Pivljanin — receives Venetian cavalry pay alongside Janković Jan 1685 (doc 44); a separate “fatto del harambassa Bajo” mentioned March 1685 (doc 57) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Demetrio (Dmitar) Nikolić-Pivljanin — 1696 granted 12 fields and ruined tower of Mustajbeg Ćerinagić in Padglivie/Trebinje as benemerito brother of late Bajo Pivljanin (doc. 287). The source’s text “figliolo” is corrected by Desnica’s footnote to “fratello” — i.e., he is Bajo’s brother, not son Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Poropat.title: Poropat
wiki/surnames/Poropat.content:
Poropat (Poropatić)
Old Vlach kindred attested in Zadar sources from late 14th c. as part of Butko Brančić’s katun Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Surname derives from the Vlach anthroponym poropat (“nomad / beskrevetnik”). Returned from Buzetski Kras to Zrmanja c. 1528. Some defected to Venetian territory 1538 (Novigrad distrikt); a long-term concentration remained on the Buzet Venetian side (Trstenik, Dane, Lanišće).
Bearers in this wiki

Jakov-Poropat-b????-Zacadje — primićur, Začađe (1528–1530)
Ivanis-Poropat-b????-Mirko — brother of Jakov, timar in Donje/Gornje Miranje
Alija-sin-Poropata-b????-Karin — Muslim convert, Karin (1528)
Husein-sin-Poropata-b????-Krupa — Muslim convert, Krupa (1528)
Jakov-Poropatic-b????-Rezane — kmet, Režane (1562)
Juraj-Poropatic-b???? — kapetan, brought Morlachs to Istria after Cyprus War
Pavko-Firultic-b????-Tornik, Vojo-Firultic-b????-Tornik, Juraj-Firultic-b????-Tornik, Milovan-Firultic-b????-Tornik — sons of Firultić, Tornik (1528)

wiki/surnames/Posedarski.title: Posedarski
wiki/surnames/Posedarski.content:
Posedarski (Benja-Posedarski)
Croatian noble kindred holding Posedarje on Novigrad more, on the original Tromeđa frontier. Continuous from the late-medieval period into the Mletačka era, ennobled and integrated into the Venetian colonnellato della nazione. The Posedarski “zlatna knjiga” and family archive are now held by knez Anton Benja-Posedarski in Zadar — extensively cited by Desnica.
Pre-1646 bearers (per Šarić)

Stjepan-Posedarski-b???? — chaplain who spoke before Pope Leo X (1519); possibly the same as the Stjepan converted to Islam.
Frane Posedarski (early 16th c.) — knez, converted to Islam.

1646–1684 bearers (per Desnica)

Frano (Francesco) Posedarski the Elder (d. 1671-01-06 in Zadar, age ~70 — doc. 185): governator → colonnello of cernide. Lost two nepoti at the 1647 Diklo / Bokanjac ambush (doc. 13). Buried Sv. Domenico Zadar.
Žorži (Zorzi) Posedarski — son of Frane the Elder; named capo di tutti li Morlacchi (general superintendent of all Venetian Morlachi) by ducal of 9 Dec 1664 (doc. 143); pay 500 ducati/year. Died 1679-07-21 at Posedarje, taken to Zadar and buried at Sv. Domenico (doc. 259). His widow appears in the 1680s correspondence.
Frano (Francesco) Posedarski the Younger — nipote of the elder Frane (and son of Žorži per doc. 232 — his father is Žorži the colonnello). Governator of Nin from 1672-03-20 (doc. 202); after Žorži’s death named capo de Morlacchi e sopraintendente delle cernide by Valier 1679-08-01 (doc. 260) — but the Senate did not approve, so Stojan Janković got the post 1681 (doc. 275 footnote). One of the four 1684 direttori over the Morlachi (doc. 395).
Pietro Posedarski — capo / capitan of cavalry (compagnia di cavalli) of Zadar; assigned to investigate the Greek-merchant murder 1671-01-14 (docs. 187, 188).
Paolo Posedarski — capitan of a Zadar compagnia paesana de fanti, posted at Ervenik 1670-08-12 (doc. 174).
Antonio Posedarski — capitan of cavalry, posted at Zara Vecchia (doc. 322, 1683).
Juraj/Žorži Posedarski — capitano d’ cavalli on the Knin campaign 1655; banished by ducal of Doge Francesco Molino for cowardice (fled the field with Battista Benzon) — doc. 92, 93.
Anton Benja-Posedarski — Zadar nobleman who in the 1930s held the family archive; not in the historical narrative but the source-fond’s custodian.

Notes

The family-archive, Posedarski Zbornik, is one of Desnica’s principal sources: it preserves Foscolo’s correspondence with Frane the Elder (the governator Possedaria of doc. 5 et seq., 1647 onward) and other otherwise-untranscribed material.
The dispatch in doc. 105 (1656-08-10) shows Žorži Posedarski lobbying to be named colonnello sopra di Morlacchi, a move Janko Mitrović and the Morlach harambaše explicitly resisted on the grounds that they would not accept a non-patrician commander.

Sources

Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre — pre-1646.
Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 5, 7–10, 13, 92, 93, 104, 105, 143, 174, 185, 187, 188, 202, 232, 259, 260, 275, 289, 322, 395.

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
The Posedarski continue as the senior Zadar-noble Morlach commanders into the 18th c.
New context for Frane (Francesco) the Younger

1689 (Cornaro Liga reform, doc. 224): family service noted.
1691-02-08 named colonnello sopraintendente of Kotari by Molin (doc. 235); both his father conte Francesco (the elder) and uncle Žorži were predecessor joint colonnelli.
1692 helped Dolfin reconcile the Mitrović and Milković parties (doc. 247).
1696 one of Liga giudici under Dolfin (doc. 286); visited Starigrad, Dračevac, Jasenice, Obrovac for Doge Valier and reported on cannon-deliveries to Karlobag (doc. 290).
1701 leased decima at Kotari (per chunk 4); 1701-06-05 challenged Zaviša Janković to oath at relics of St. Šimun (doc. 330).
1701-09-10 sent on diplomatic mission to Bosnian Pasha with extensive gift list to Halil-pasha (doc. 333).
1702 served Lisičić–Brgud arbitration. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

New bearer

conte Pietro Posedarski — nobile zaratino, age 43 in 1699 (b. ~1656); witness re Morlacca possession in Sfakioto’s Grimani-commission protocols (doc. 315). Probable brother or cousin of Frane the Younger. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Family note

Per Molin’s 1691 doc. 235: the new colonnello Francesco is “figlio e nipote respective de medemi” — son of conte Francesco the Elder and nephew of his fratello conte Žorži. Both elder brothers were joint colonnelli. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

wiki/surnames/Punos.title: Punos
wiki/surnames/Punos.content:
Punoš

wiki/surnames/Radmilovic.title: Radmilovic
wiki/surnames/Radmilovic.content:

Bukovica surname attested in Žegar.
Bearers attested

Mihajlo Radmilović — Morlach who escaped from Žegar to Venetian territory; goods stolen in transit by villagers of Razanci (Marko Matak) and Radovin (Ivan Brkljača and Giacomo Bistrić); ordered restored by Mocenigo (doc 31, 1684). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Notes

Per Desnica’s 1951 editorial footnote (to doc 115), the Radmilović surname is still present in Žegar today (1951). Together with Zelić, Vukčević, and Nanić, the families “came in 1648 with the Jankovićs to Budim near Posedarje and during the Morean War many returned to Lika; Budim is today (1951) ruins”. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

wiki/surnames/Rkac.content:

Bearers

wiki/surnames/Rosic.title: Rosic
wiki/surnames/Rosic.content:
Rošić
Bearers

wiki/surnames/Rudelic.title: Rudelic
wiki/surnames/Rudelic.content:
Rudelić (Rudelja)
Pre-Ottoman Vlachs of the wider Zadar hinterland Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Toponyms Rudele (Kistanje) and Rodaljica reflect their old katun. By 1528 a small dzemat under Pavel-Rudelja-b????-Obrovac in nahija Obrovac. Branches migrated to Rovinjsko Selo in Istria (village judges) and Radovin in Zadar district; from Radovin in 1683 to Karlobag and Šugarje, with some to Smiljan in Lika.
Bearers in this wiki

Pavel-Rudelja-b????-Obrovac — knez, primićur Obrovac dzemat (1528)
Pavo-Rudelic-b????-Smiljan — Smiljan, Lika (1686)

wiki/surnames/Rukavina.title: Rukavina
wiki/surnames/Rukavina.content:
Rukavina
Major Bunjevac lineage of Lika and Podgorje. The family preserves an oral genealogy tracing its origin to the Vladimirovići of Hum — a noble line said to have been driven out of Raška by the Nemanjići. Šarić treats this as a “raška reminiscencija” reflecting how Bunjevac elite memory absorbed early-Hercegovinian “raško razdoblje” rather than a literal medieval pedigree (the legend was nourished by 18th-c. baroque Slavism and Kačić Miošić’s pjesmarica) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Documented presence

Pre-Candian War — Rukavine were starešine of catholic Morlachs in Jasenica in Morlakija (per Forza 1636 supplementary information cited by Šarić) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
1691 — granted estates by Habsburg authorities in Sv-Mihovil, Sv-Rok, Vratnik, Ricice, Kosinj as part of the Bunjevac influx into recovered Lika (Fras 1835).
1712 Lika–Krbava popis — Rukavina present in the parishes of Budak, Ribnik, Udbina (Lika regiment); Perušić, Kompolje (Otočac regiment); Drežnik-grad, Vaganac (Ogulin regiment).

Andrija Kačić Miošić’s 1756 pjesmarica names Rukavine among “vitezovi hrvatski” alongside Starcevic, Balenovic and Dosen — illustrating the surname’s military prominence by mid-18th c. Saric-2008-Bunjevci

wiki/surnames/Rusic.title: Rusic
wiki/surnames/Rusic.content:
Rušić (Rusić)
Hercegovinian Catholic family from Mostar district.
Bearers in Desnica II

Ivan Rašić/Rušić (Giovanni Rassich) — from Rusić village (near Mostar); Catholic; led 200 souls / 25 families from Mostar district to Makarska area; settled Zavojane, Stigli, Hadži Lukovo on lands of late Salin-aga Đikić; appointed harambaša Oct 1692 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 258).
Šimun Rusić (Simon Rusich) dalla Torretta (Tornik) — named arbitrator by Lisičić/Podgrađe side in 1702 dispute with Brgud (doc. 348) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Ruzic.title: Ruzic
wiki/surnames/Ruzic.content:
Ružić
Vlach kindred originating from Šibenik area, members of the medieval “kraljevski Vlasi” (royal Vlachs) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Migrated to Vodice on Kras 1518; returned to nahija Kličevac (Miranje, Jagodnja) under Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik 1528. After 1538/40 returned to Šibenik area; 1540 morlački katun “Ružić”, with katunar Jure-Heracic-b???? in 1553.
Bearers in this wiki

Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik — knez, head of Kličevac dzemat (1528–~1538)
Jure-Heracic-b???? — katunar of Ružić katun (1553)

wiki/surnames/Ruzzini.content:

wiki/surnames/Salentich.content:

wiki/surnames/Sarcevic.title: Sarcevic
wiki/surnames/Sarcevic.content:
Šarčević
Bačka variant of Šarić. Foremost member: Boza-Sarcevic-b????-Subotica (Ambrozije Šarčević) — launched the Bunjevački kalendar in Subotica in 1868, foundational publication of the 19th-c. Bunjevac narodni preporod alongside Ivan-Antunovic-b1815-Backa’s 1870 Bunjevačke i šokačke novine in Kaloča Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

wiki/surnames/Saric.title: Saric
wiki/surnames/Saric.content:
Šarić
Surname documented in vlach/Bunjevac milieu of the Tromeđa from the 17th c. onward. The major kotarski uskočka branch is Šibenik-based pravoslavna, centered on serdar Cvijan/Cvitko Šarić (active 1647–1668+).
Bearers in this wiki

Cvijan-Saric-b????-Sibenik — serdar šibenskih pravoslavnih Morlaka 1647–1668+; recorded 1660 by Evlija Çelebi as “hrvatski razbojnik” Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Wife Dessa. See his page for the multi-generational genealogy.
Iuan/Ivan Šarić — son of Cvijan & Dessa; baptised 1654-07-02 Sv. Zulijan Šibenik (docs. 81, 83 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).
Žorži (Zorzi) Šarić — harambassa in 1654 Sv. Zulijan parish protest list (doc. 84).
Zuanne/Jovan Šarić — son of Cvijan; family pay transferred to him 1662-03-14 by Korner (doc. 123); back-pay arrears settled by ducal of Doge Alvise Contarini 1682-06-03 (doc. 285).
Đeno Sarić (1842) — early recorder of the Buna-river origin legend, who wrote that the “stara postojbina Bunjevaca” was on the Buna Saric-2008-Bunjevci (no separate page).
Marko-Saric-b????-Zagreb — modern historian, author of Saric-2008-Bunjevci and Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

The 1868-launched Subotica Bunjevački kalendar of Boza-Sarcevic-b????-Subotica is the same surname in its Šarčević variant — bačka spelling of Šarić Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Ibrahim Sarić (Ibrahim Sarich) da Cliuno (Livno) — slave; testified about Knin cadi jurisdiction over Strmica, Bošnjake, Komazlić, Golubić, Starčević etc. (doc. 315, 1699) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Sbizza.content:
Sbizza

quartier mastro Luca Sbizza — compare of Marija Smiljanić; executor and legatee in her 1693 will; testimon (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Scutari.content:

wiki/surnames/Segotic.content:

Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

wiki/surnames/Selakovic.title: Selakovic
wiki/surnames/Selakovic.content:
Selaković
Bearers

Iviša Selaković da Scardona, habitante a Visovaz — 1647-12-17 in Šibenik signs (with X) the Petropolje uskakanje contract (doc. 18 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).

Barba e mustacchi castagni, occhi uarii, pel oscuro. Segno sopra la tempia sinistra” (doc. 23). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

wiki/surnames/Sikic.content:

Morlach colonist family in southern Istria. 1586: Sime-Sikic-b???? and Mate-Sikic-b???? founded the Šikići hamlet near Pula — first attested “bunjevačka” stream into southern Istra Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

Sime-Sikic-b???? — Šikići founder (1586)
Mate-Sikic-b???? — Šikići founder (1586)

Sikirić

wiki/surnames/Siljanovic.title: Siljanovic
wiki/surnames/Siljanovic.content:
Šiljanović (Siglanović)
Istrian Vlach starešina Rade-Siljanovic-b???? led peasants to former Vrana district as zakup on Venetian land in 1549 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Possible but unconfirmed continuity with the medieval kraljevski Vlach katun Šiglanovići of Knin županija (14th c.).
Bearers in this wiki

Rade-Siljanovic-b???? — Vlach starešina, settler-leader (1549)

wiki/surnames/Sincevic.title: Sincevic
wiki/surnames/Sincevic.content:
Sinčević
Bearers

Grubiša Sinčević (father) and Žorži Sinčević (son) — 1684-01-24 hold 4 gold rings, 1 silver ring, 9 silver buttons, gold collana with 8 perusini and 250 pearls — Krivelari pawn jewellery later raided (doc. 366).
Gregorio Cusinovich detto Sian (1684-01-24, doc. 366) — susach worth 5 reali — possibly the same family.

wiki/surnames/Sinobad.title: Sinobad
wiki/surnames/Sinobad.content:
Sinobad
Budin (Ravni Kotari) capitanska family. Per Desnica’s footnote on doc. 181: in 1684-07-01 Mocenigo granted Jovan Sinobad the kula at Karin when he settled the area with Morlaci from Modrino Selo; the kula is still standing and known as “Sinobaduša.”
Bearers

Pera (Periza, Petar) Sinobad — kapetan di Budin (per doc. 279 his son Jovan is called “figlia [sic, figliolo] del capitano di Budin”). Killed by Ilija Mitrović with his band; houses burned in Budin (doc. 396).
Jovan (Zuanne) Sinobadović = “Zuan Sinobad” — son of Pera; alive 1682-02-17 (doc. 279, deposing about Ćosić’s sheep); 1683-12-26 attests in the murder/plunder by Ilija Mitrović and others of his father and brother (doc. 391, 396); subsequently received the Karin kula.
(1684 unnamed brother) — also killed by Ilija Mitrović’s band.
uncle of Jovan — 1684 prevented from cultivating the family lands by Ilija Mitrović (doc. 396).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
The Sinobad family rises across the Morean War period to become the principal Venetian Morlach kapetanska family of the Knin–Zvonigrad region. Major figures span four generations.
Genealogy (per Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II)

Petar (Pietro/Pera) Sinobad of Posedarje — killed at Brgud at start of Morean War by Radan Matić of Brgud (doc. 331); blood vendetta carried by son Jovan into 1701 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Jovan / Zuanne Sinobad (kavalier) — son of Petar; appointed governor of Zvonigrad 1690-05-24 with company of 50 paesani, salary 14 ducats (doc. 234); appointed governor of Knin krajina 1691-06-20 with 60 fields and vineyards near Bulin Most plus houses in Knin from late Turks Hadži-Kurtović, Hadži-Emorić, Acmet-aga Livaković (docs. 239, 241); reconciled with Mitrović family 1692 (doc. 247); house in Modrino selo, Bukovica, near St. Peter’s church 1692 (doc. 259, casale of Turk Modre, his congiunto); appointed sopraintendente of Knin krajina 1696-10-16 (doc. 293); cavalier of San Marco 1696-01-30 by Doge Valier (Sinj, Čitluk, Klivno) (doc. 283). Died 1715 in Glamoč clash (doc. 372). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Filippo Sinobad — alfier then capitano of Zvonigrad; brother of Jovan; appointed June 1691 to replace Jovan; died before Aug 1694 (docs. 240, 277).
Mihail (Michiel) Sinobad — nephew of Jovan and Filippo; previously held tower of Topolje; appointed captain of Zvonigrad 1694-08-21 to succeed late Filippo (doc. 277); died ~1697, replaced by Andrea (doc. 304). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Andrea (Andrija) Sinobad — son of kavalier Jovan; appointed captain of Zvonigrad company 1697 as a child with tutor “governatore” on father’s merit (doc. 304); later serdar of Knin; died 1725 (referenced 1726, doc. 376). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Giacomo (Jakov) Sinobad — cornetta riformato; cousin of deceased Andrea Sinobad; “ultimo superstite della famiglia”; supplicated 1727 to be made serdar of Knin per family tradition; appointed serdar Knin 1729-12-01 by Vendramin replacing Petar Mitrović-Stojisavljević (docs. 378, 380). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Gvozden Sinobad — uncle (“zio”) of kavalier Jovan; ordered 1699 to return cloak with silver to Anđelija Krišanova Kolundžija (doc. 313). Distinct from Gvozden Radasović. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
The unnamed nephew (sister’s son) of Jovan — leader of haiduks on Mt. Prolog with Vid Petrović and 60 men; attacked Ottoman travellers and a village near Atlagić tower 1702 (doc. 346). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Houses, lands, slaves

Modrino selo, Bukovica — village named after Turk Modre, congiunto of Sinobad; casale assigned to Jovan 1692; later disputed 1697 with Radoš and Sava Kresović who refused to return (docs. 259, 302). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Knin Turkish properties — houses of Acmet-aga Livaković, Hadži-Kurtović, Hadži-Emorić; 60 fields near Bulin Most + Aqua Radeglievaz (doc. 241).
Slave Seifulah of Travnik — confessed in 1702 ransom of 200 reali, silver saber, silver horse-tack (doc. 343).

Notes

The old feud between casa Mitrović and casa Sinobad (“engami implacabili”) was reconciled by Dolfin in 1692; Sinobad moved to Knin to physically separate the two houses Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 247).
Family origin: Posedarje. Ancestors had worked under Turks at Modrino selo (doc. 259).

wiki/surnames/Sinovcic.title: Sinovcic
wiki/surnames/Sinovcic.content:
Sinovčić
Bearers

Tomo Sinovčić — of Novigrad (Dalmatia); rewarded by Mocenigo on 5 September 1684 for killing 5 Turks at Grahovo plus the kjehaja (lieutenant) of Mazut-paša (doc 32 footnote) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Tomaso Sinovčić — from Novigrad; complained-against by Obrovac inhabitants for taking lands across the river 1690 (doc. 230) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Likely the same man as 1684.

wiki/surnames/Skulic.title: Skulic
wiki/surnames/Skulic.content:
Škulić
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers (Desnica)
Two Ražanac members killed at the Otres battle 1662-02-13 (doc. 119 — Ražanačka godovna knjiga):

Grubiša Škulić
Ivan Škulić

wiki/surnames/Sladovic.title: Sladovic
wiki/surnames/Sladovic.content:
Sladović
Catholic Vlach (Bunjevac) lineage — third of the three core Bunjevac katuns named in the 1477 defter (with Krmpotic and Vojnic). Least documented of the three.
1477 attestation
Hercegovina defter, nahija Mostar: džemat of Milosav-sin-Sladica-b????-Mostar, 19 houses. Unusually for the 1477 popis, the džemat is organized by villages (Podci = Podaca in Makarsko primorje; Igre = Igrane on Biokovo; Kozica in Vrgoračka krajina) rather than by transhumant pastures. This suggests either “vlahizirano” sedentary peasants given Vlach status, or a fully territorialized Vlach katun Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
17th c. — westward migration
Early 17th c.: present across Bukovica and Podgorje under vojvoda Gvozden-Sladovic-b????-Mostar; group known as “Gvozdenovi ljudi”. 1605: 20 families joined the Krmpote migration to Lic — surnames Balinović, Brošković, Ilnić, Karanović, Lovrić, Martinović, Mihovilović, Mikulić, Sladović, Veljanić, Vilenica.
After 1605 the group’s fate intertwined with the Krmpote branch. Some Sladovići joined the Senjska-Kapetanija garrison; a Senj-line branch later settled in Licko-Lesce (Otočac). The historian Manojlo-Sladovic-b????-Lika (1856 Pověsti biskupijah Senjske i Modruške) probably descends from this branch Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Bearers in this wiki

Milosav-sin-Sladica-b????-Mostar — 1477 katun head
Gvozden-Sladovic-b????-Mostar — vojvoda, early 17th c.
Manojlo-Sladovic-b????-Lika — historian (1856)

wiki/surnames/Smiljanic.title: Smiljanic
wiki/surnames/Smiljanic.content:
Smiljanić — poreklom iz Udbine
One of the senior kotarski uskočki lineages, with multi-generational prominence. Originally from Udbina, not Smiljan — Desnica’s correction is critical and overrides the legend.
Genealogy

Petar Smiljanić (founder; d. 1648-07-17 at Ribnik): had two armed sons — Ilija and Filip.
Ilija Smiljanić (b. ~1622, d. 1654-09-08 at Vučjak): serdar; childless? — widow Kata remarried Milivoj Zubičević 1655.
Filip Smiljanić (b. ~1633, d. Jan 1656 in a Šibenik brawl): kapetan; killed before producing heirs.
Smoljan Smiljanić (a/k/a Smoglianovich, also Mihalevich): nephew (nipote) of Ilija and Filip; serdar from 1664; heir of the family pay; uterine half-brother of Šimun and Marko Brajinović (their mother Anka had a first marriage to Frane Brajinović of Spianata-behind-Sv. Marko).

Lazaro Smiljanić (in tenera età 1679): son of Smoljan; capitan of a 50-man company.



Bearers attested in this source

Petar Smiljanić — d. Ribnik 1648.
Ilija Smiljanić — d. Vučjak 1654.
Filip Smiljanić — d. Šibenik 1656; alfier Frane Marininić killed with him.
Smoljan Smiljanić (Smoglianovich) — serdar; kavalier; commandant of Nadin.
Lazaro Smiljanić — capitan, 1679 (doc. 255).
Bartulo Banenović da Pavičići — Germano del carambassà Elia Smiglianich (doc. 66, 1652-10-05) — a kinsman of Ilija ransomed by him.
Kata — Turkish-born wife of Ilija, remarried Milivoj Zubičević (Šibenik). Their son Lukas Zubičević was b. 1665-10-15.

Notes

The Smiljanići of Udbina led the Bukovčani uskakanje — Petar (1648), then his sons Ilija and Filip in succession.
The legend of “Smiljanić Ilija” / “Filip Smiljanić” / “Vuk Smiljanić” in epic poetry goes back to this family but is layered over historical fact.

Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 20 (and footnote 1 for the Udbina correction), 36, 38, 41, 42, 53, 66, 71, 72, 75, 86, 87, 88, 89, 97, 98, 99, 103, 139, 144, 163, 165, 166, 184, 190, 255, 395.

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Smiljanić family continues prominently through Morean War and into 18th c.; widow Marija (née Bolić) and son Lazaro provide the testamentary archive.
New bearers and contexts

Marko Smiljanić — capitano; brother of Smoljan; awarded 10 ducats/month 1690-05-21 by Doge Morosini for service in the Morean campaigns (Calamata, Navarino, Modon, Napoli di Romania, Negroponte, Malvasia) (doc. 233). Died 1693-02-23 aged ~46 (b. ~1647) in Zadar; given last unction by don Andrea Caldana; buried San Domenico (doc. 264). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Marija Smiljanić (née Bolić) — widow of Smoljan Smiljanić; testament in Zadar 1693-10-05; died between then and 1694-04-13 when will opened; buried San Domenico; mother of Lazaro and Margarita; sister-in-law of Marko (doc. 267). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Lazzaro (Lazaro) Smiljanić — son of Smoljan and Marija; heir per Marija’s will; wrote his own will 1696-07-28 leaving estate to wife Maria (Bolić) and unborn child, alternately to slaves and Dominicans; commended at siege of Ulcinj 1696 (docs. 267, 289, 299). 1700 supplicated to be made serdar — claimed he was last surviving member of Smiljanić family (doc. 320, with footnote noting supplica’s exaggerations: Filip actually killed in Šibenik brawl 1656, not by Turks; Smoljan’s death at Sinj not corroborated). Eventually appointed serdar of Lower Kotari (succeeding Bože Milković after his ~1700 death); led troops to Italy 1702 (replaced provisionally by Antonio Vujanović); died ~early 1709 (docs. 320, 322, 323, 338, 352, 367, 368, 377). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Maria Bolić-Smiljanić — wife of Lazzaro Smiljanić; pregnant when he wrote will 1696 (doc. 289). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Margarita Smiglianich — daughter of Smoljan and Marija; living 1693 (doc. 267); married a “Salentich governor” who received green velvet jacket bequest. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Marko Smiljanić (the younger) — minor son of Lazar Smiljanić; reserved as serdar of Lower Kotari 1709-02-20 by Vendramin; held captaincy of paesana company in terraferma (docs. 367, 368, 377). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Aloisi (nephew of Marija Smiljanić) — bequeathed silver buttons (doc. 267).
Giovanni / Zuanne (other nephew of Marija) — bequeathed silk sash (doc. 267).
Smiljanić (governor) — one of three serdars sent to negotiate with rebellious Bukovica Morlachi 1704 alongside Gvozden Radasović and Spingaroli (doc. 352) — likely Lazar.

Notes

Per supplica footnote in doc. 320: Filip’s death was in a Šibenik brawl with Venetian soldiers (drunk), not killed by Turks as Lazaro claimed. Smoljan’s claimed death at conquest of Sinj is also doubted by editor.
Marija’s testament debtors include don Gregorio Begna (4 zecchini); recipients include Caterina Pizzocara, Vincenza Pastrović, padre Scutari (provinciale Dominican), Ellena daughter of dottor Cassio (diamond ring), her compare quartier mastro Luca Sbizza.
Notary: Andreas de Toris; consigliere/giudice: Biagio Soppe; commissario: Casseretti; conte di Zara: Giovanni Mirelli (doc. 267).

wiki/surnames/Smirich.content:
Smirich

wiki/surnames/Sojat.title: Sojat
wiki/surnames/Sojat.content:
Šojat
Bunjevac surname; among the 16 reconstructed families of the 1627 Krmpote migration (Pavličević 1989) Saric-2008-Bunjevci (medium confidence). 1712 popis: present in Priboj parish (Otočac regiment).

wiki/surnames/Sokolic.title: Sokolic
wiki/surnames/Sokolic.content:
Sokolić
Bearers in Desnica II

Toni Francesco Sokolić — still alive at time of Peri’s report 1695; collected dues at Starigrad and Jablanac during last Frankopans’ time (doc. 281) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Sokolovic.title: Sokolovic
wiki/surnames/Sokolovic.content:
Sokolović
Bosnian Ottoman beylik family. Ferhat-beg-Sokolovic-b???? served as kliški sandžakbeg, settled ~200 Istrian Vlach families in Knin area 1568, and uvakufio Tinj (1574) for the Zemunik vakuf with Vojnić Bunjevac colonists Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Ferhat-beg-Sokolovic-b???? — kliški sandžakbeg (1568+)

wiki/surnames/Solimano.title: Solimano
wiki/surnames/Solimano.content:
Solimano
Bearers

captain Solimano — captain of light cavalry Feb 1685 (doc 51); Italian rendering of Sulayman — bearer possibly a convert from Islam in Venetian service Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Soppe.title: Soppe
wiki/surnames/Soppe.content:
Šope (Soppe)
Zadar patrician family with multiple branches active over the period.
Bearers

Petar (Pero) Šope (Soppe) — governator, capitano equitum of Zadar; 1655-02-25 banished by ducal of Doge Molino for cowardice at the Knin battle (doc. 92, 93).
knez Julio (Giulio) Soppe — capitano delle ville littorali. Active across 1683–84: 1683-10-23 leads the company that at Bokanjac–Boccagnazzo turned back the looters; burned the houses of 4 ringleaders (doc. 322). 1683-12-09 with col. Posedarski sent to investigate (doc. 348). 1684-03-01 governator of Zaravecchia (doc. 381). One of the four 1684 direttori (doc. 395).
Giovanni Battista Soppe Fortezza, kavalier — 1668-12-09 leads the Bribir ambush as direttore (doc. 163, 165). 1679 (undated) sent by Valier to Žemunik to confer with Hasan-beg Durakbegović and the krčki kadi (doc. 261).
Biagio (Biasio) Sope dottore — 1682-11-06 nominated for the Liga oversight (doc. 296).
Simon Sope — 1682-11-06 same source.

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

conte Giulio (Julio) Soppe — consigliere in Zadar, witness to the 14 September 1686 Stojan-Janković purchase contract (doc 143); also serving as one of the four 1684 direttori (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
kavalier Giovan Battista Soppe Fortezza — appears across the early Morean War correspondence (docs 15, 19, 24, 32) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Biagio Soppe, dottor — consigliere of corte di Zara, executor of Marija Smiljanić’s 1693 testament (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Giovanni Battista Soppe Fortezza, magnifico signor governator — nobile zaratino consigliere 1701; co-owner of half of Olib island (the other half sold by conte Giacomo Califfi to Zaviša Mitrović 1701-11-26, doc. 336) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Soric.title: Soric
wiki/surnames/Soric.content:
Sorić
Catholic Vlach surname, Zadar-hinterland origin. Šarić lists it among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. The line straddles the 1636 župnik through to the Vrana uprising 1683.
Bearers

don Stjepan (Stipan) Sorić — 1636 župnik in Gorica/Tinj parish; 1647 governator de Morlacchi; killed at Ribnik 1648-07-17. See Stipan-Soric-b????-Gorica for full bio.
Mate Sorić — brother of don Stjepan; succeeded him 1648-07-31 as Goričanski capo; received the gold chain originally meant for Stjepan.
Gregorio Sorić — 1683 implied as relative pursuing recovery of pop Stjepan’s preserved hand from Margarita Ivančević (doc. 311).
pop Stevan Sorić of Tepšinci — 1684-03-23 with knez of Tepšinci and Parčići (Lika), pleads to provveditore Donà for asylum and bread for the would-be migrant Lika families; wants to be settled at Obrovac (donji + gornji), per his Cyrillic letter (doc. 385). NOT obviously the same family but the pop Stevan / pop Stjepan coincidence in the same diocese is suggestive.

Notes

The same surname appears among the Šibenik pravoslavni Morlaci — Steffano Sare harambašša at Sv. Zulijan (doc. 84, 1654) — but Sare may be distinct from Sorić, hard to pin down.

wiki/surnames/Sorini.title: Sorini
wiki/surnames/Sorini.content:
Sorini
Bearers

abbate Sorini — abbot, present as witness in the cancelleria civil pretoria of Zadar (doc at line 4134, 1685) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Spachioto.title: Spachioto
wiki/surnames/Spachioto.content:
Spachioto
Bearers

Nicolò Spachioto — witness in the Zadar cancelleria civil pretoria alongside abbate Sorini (doc at line 4135, 1685) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Spingaroli.title: Spingaroli
wiki/surnames/Spingaroli.content:
Spingaroli
Zadar noble; long-serving Venetian governator.
Bearers in Desnica II

Francesco Spingaroli — appointed governor of pertinenza 9 (Zaravecchia) by Cornaro in 1689 Liga reform (doc. 224); reappointed governor of Biograd, Pakoštane and Vrana by Dolfin March 1694 (doc. 275); helped at sieges of Castelnuovo and Knin (doc. 286). Age 32 in 1699 (b. ~1667), testified in Sfakioto’s protocols (doc. 315); supplied 25 sessane and 8 horses for Grimani 1699 (doc. 314); in 1704 one of three serdars sent to negotiate with rebellious Bukovica Morlacchi (with Gvozden Radasović and Smiljanić, doc. 352); 1726 governor of Zaravecchia for Lower Kotari (doc. 377) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Spolverino.title: Spolverino
wiki/surnames/Spolverino.content:
Spolverino
Bearers

conte collonello Spolverino — distinguished himself in the early actions at the 1686 Sinj-Salona campaign (lines 6457, 6467) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Stanisic.title: Stanisic
wiki/surnames/Stanisic.content:
Stanišić
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Zorzi (Đurađ) Stanković (Stancovich) — Gorica resident; goods stolen in 1693-11-04 raid; recognized Žegar dialect of raiders (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Surname spelled Stanković in the source.
See also separate Stojanović entry.

Note: a Nikanor Stanković of Velika appears at Šaramprov of Kalinika 1698, protected from Bishop Busović’s harassment (doc. 308) — surname Stanković, possibly distinct from Stanišić Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Stankovic.content:
Stanković
Bearers in Desnica II

Zorzi (Đurađ) Stanković (Stancovich) — Gorica resident; goods stolen in 1693-11-04 raid; recognized Žegar dialect of raiders (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Nikanor Stanković (Nichinor Stancouich) — from Velika; location Šaramprov of Kalinika; protected from Bishop Nikodim Busović’s harassment 1698 (doc. 308) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Starcevic.title: Starcevic
wiki/surnames/Starcevic.content:
Starčević
Bunjevac lineage that became one of the most consequential families in 19th-c. Croatian political history. The surname appears in the 1627 (second) Krmpote migration to Lic Saric-2008-Bunjevci; settled in Veliki Žitnik / Pazarište after the 1690 colonization of Lika.
Lika progenitor and the Bunjevačka buna
Porkulab Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik (1656–?) settled at Pazariste in 1690. Per the 1712 popis (Kaser 2003), he held 168 štrikova (parcels) in Pazarište, Vaganac, and Žitnik, with one son Jakov (age 20) and five other family members.
His conflict with vojvoda Marko-Butorac-b????-Lika in 1702 sparked the Ribnicka-Buna-1702 (also “Bunjevačka buna”).
Lika regiment officers (mid-18th c.)
Miloš’s sons Jakov-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste and Matija-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste became kapetani in the newly formed Lika regiment in 1746. Andrija Kačić Miošić, in Razgovor ugodni naroda slovinskoga (1756), celebrated Jakov among the “vitezovi hrvatski” — early evidence that Bunjevac kin in Lika were absorbing a Hrvatski (regimental/zemaljski) identity Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
The grammarian and the founder of HSP

Jakov’s grandson Filip-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste — village knez at end of 18th c.
Filip’s son Sime-Starcevic-b1784-Lika (1784–1859) — priest and grammarian, promoter of “zemaljski” / “pučki” hrvatstvo.
Šime’s nephew Ante-Starcevic-b1823-Veliki-Zitnik (1823–1896) — founder of modern Croatian etnonacionalni identity (Hrvatska stranka prava).

The Klan Starčevića continued in the political work of David and Mile Starčević. Šarić uses the lineage as the paradigmatic case of how Lika Bunjevci absorbed a modern Croatian national identity within a single century Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Note on confessional drift
The 1712 popis lists Starčević as a surname shared between Bunjevci (Catholic) and Orthodox Vlasi in Lika–Krbava — one of 37 such overlapping surnames documenting common Dinaric origin Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Bearers in this wiki

Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik — porkulab Pazarišta, 1702 buna
Jakov-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste — Lika regiment kapetan, 1746
Matija-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste — Lika regiment kapetan, 1746
Filip-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste — knez (late 18th c.)
Sime-Starcevic-b1784-Lika — priest, grammarian
Ante-Starcevic-b1823-Veliki-Zitnik — founder of HSP

wiki/surnames/Stipcevic.content:
Stipčević

wiki/surnames/Stojanovic.title: Stojanovic
wiki/surnames/Stojanovic.content:
Stojanović
Bearers

Constadin (Kostadin) Stojanović of Oton — 1652-10-05 Turkish-subject slave on the galley of Antonio Barbaro; offered as ransom for Bartul Banenović of Pavičići (Ilija Smiljanić’s germano) (doc. 66).
Mihovil Stojanović — 1684-03-01 named capitano of Pakoštani (doc. 381).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Nikola Stojanović (Nicolo Stoianovich) — courier; named in 1734 as messenger to forward money to imprisoned pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža in Venetian Pozzi/Camerotti prisons (doc. 385) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Stoljic.title: Stoljic
wiki/surnames/Stoljic.content:
Stiljić
Single attestation: Jurašin Stiljić, novi habitant Posedarja — 1663-05-08 ordered by Contarini to be brought before him by force if necessary by the kotari sudci Mirko Knežević, Stojan Mitrović, Pavle Vučević, Milinko Barićević (doc. 131).

wiki/surnames/Strmic.title: Strmic
wiki/surnames/Strmic.content:
Strmić
Bearers

Matija (Mattio) Strmić — member of the Radoš consortium that owned Hasan-beg Mandić as slave (doc 65) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Sudarovic.title: Sudarovic
wiki/surnames/Sudarovic.content:
Sudarović
Bearers

Jovan (Zuanne) Sudarović of Parčići — Lika Morlach harambaša with c. 150–300 men under arms, settled in Karlobag and upper Obrovac on the Habsburg side. The Imperial commissar (a Karlović) tried to retain him with the offer of life-tenure as captain of Karlobag plus privileges, but Sudarović preferred Venice; on 23 November 1685 (doc 114) appeared with his companion Rade Rkać before Pietro Valier in Split and proposed to settle in the abandoned Žegar castle with a paid 100-man company plus food provisions until harvest, bringing a small cannon captured from the Udbina Turks. Awarded 4 cecchini for travel and sent back to Janković and the cavalry provveditor Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Sugaric.title: Sugaric
wiki/surnames/Sugaric.content:
Šugarić
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Šugarje in Podgorje is the relocation site for Rudelic families from Radovin in 1683.

wiki/surnames/Susic.title: Susic
wiki/surnames/Susic.content:
Šušić
Bearers

harambaša Radivoj Šušić — 1648-07-17: “Uskoci iz Ugaraka naseljeni u Žeravi od 60 ljudi izgubili trojicu” at Ribnik (doc. 39 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).
Martin Suskovich da Budin — 1683-12-16 missing after the Pađen-Knin battle, possibly killed (doc. 353); 1684-04-07 in the Sinobad case complainants list (doc. 391).

wiki/surnames/Sutic.title: Sutic
wiki/surnames/Sutic.content:
Šutić
Single attestation: fra Grga (Gregorio) Šutić — Bosnian Franciscan; 1683-11 reports to Donà his secret meeting with the rebel knez Ilija da Radassinovzi, conte Marko Klarić of Stankovci, harambaša Martin Đagnimić and harambaša Idero (Ždero) at the village Uselize sopra Vrana — pivotal document for the Vrana uprising (doc. 333).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)

fra Grgur Šutić — continues to act as Bosnian Franciscan cappellano / mediator; appears in the 1684 Vrana petitions to Mocenigo and in the post-rising negotiations (docs 34, 36) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Svetacki.title: Svetacki
wiki/surnames/Svetacki.content:
Svetački
Slavonian noble lineage, members entered Ottoman service in 1540 — example of frontier elite ambivalent loyalties (Mujadžević 2023, cited by Šarić) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

wiki/surnames/Tadic.title: Tadic
wiki/surnames/Tadic.content:
Tadić
Bearers

knez Nikola Tadijić — 1648-07-17 uskočki leader: “Uskoci iz Krmpote naseljeni ispod Poljica, od 150 pješaka izgubili 10” at the Battle of Ribnik (doc. 39 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).
Nicolo Tadich da Carpote — 1653-01-16 same individual; co-signs the proxy authorising Ilija Smiljanić to plead the Morlachi case in Venice (doc. 70).
Tadić (capitan) of Starigrad — owner of Mlin del conte Tadijch in the perimeter of the 1679 land allocation to the Sv. Juraj uskoks (doc. 258).

wiki/surnames/Tagga.title: Tagga
wiki/surnames/Tagga.content:
Tagga
Single attestation: captain of Knin Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 224 context). Stub page.

wiki/surnames/Tanusi.title: Tanusi
wiki/surnames/Tanusi.content:
Tanusi
Likely an Albanian / Oltremarini surname (cf. the medieval Albanian tribe Tanushi).
Bearers

major Tanusi — major in the Oltremarini; killed at the Sinj defeat April 1685 (docs 17, 60) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Tardic.title: Tardic
wiki/surnames/Tardic.content:
Tardić (Gajdić)
Croatian-Šibenik lineage of Murat-beg-Gajdic-b????-Sibenik (formerly Tardić), the first sanjakbeg of Sandzak-Klis. Old surname Tardić; the Ottoman variant “Gajdić” appears alongside it in sources. Origin and Šibenik kin documented in Juran 2016 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Murat-beg-Gajdic-b????-Sibenik — subaša/voivod of Vilajet Hrvati, first sanjakbeg of Klis

wiki/surnames/Tartaglia.title: Tartaglia
wiki/surnames/Tartaglia.content:
Tartaglia
Trogir/Kaštela-area officer family.
Bearers

Pietro Tartaglia — officer at Duare (Zadvarje) 1685; co-signatory with Geliseo and Razzetini of dispatches to Valier from the Castelli of Traù (docs 60, and lines 4522, 4586) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Tepsic.title: Tepsic
wiki/surnames/Tepsic.content:
Tepšić
Bearers

Rade Tepšić — Lika Morlach resident in Zadar city; January 1686 brought legal action against Ostoja Gagić of Biljane for an unliquidated debt; agreed to release Gagić under bail (doc 124, 29 Jan 1686) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Tiepolo.title: Tiepolo
wiki/surnames/Tiepolo.content:
Tiepolo

provveditor Tiepolo — earlier provveditor de cavalli who had Gorica burnt because 10 banditi were there; recalled retrospectively in 1693 (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Tintic.title: Tintic
wiki/surnames/Tintic.content:
Tintić
Single attestation: fra Petar (Piero) Tintić — capellano da Petropoglie. 1683-12-09 envoy of harambaša Matija Nakić and the conti of Petropolje (1000 households) to provveditore Donà, asking either war declaration or guidance how to be protected from Venetian-side raids (doc. 349).

wiki/surnames/Tintor.title: Tintor
wiki/surnames/Tintor.content:

Gerolamo Tomadelli — signed for Zaviša Mitrović because Zaviša couldn’t write Italian (doc. 279) — Zaviša signed in Cyrillic only Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Tomasoni.title: Tomasoni
wiki/surnames/Tomasoni.content:

Francesco Tomasoni — owned a botteghetta (small shop) in Obrovac 1696 (doc. 290) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Possibly = the merchant Tomasoni of Zadar referenced in Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I doc. 234.

wiki/surnames/Tomicic.title: Tomicic
wiki/surnames/Tomicic.content:

Bearers

harambaša Martin Tomičić — 1648-07-17: “Uskoci iz Drvenika naseljeni kod Nina od 100 ljudi izgubili petoricu” at Ribnik (doc. 39 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).

Notes

The same name Tomicich is one of three sub-villages of Rudopolje in Lika that don Sorić burned in 1648-06-18 (with Vodena Glava and Pancino selo — doc. 32). Whether Martin Tomičić’s family stem from this Lika locality is plausible but not directly attested.

Andrea Tomišić (Andrija Tomišić) — killed by Ilija Janković in 1692; from Gorica (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Tomljanovic.title: Tomljanovic
wiki/surnames/Tomljanovic.content:

Bunjevac surname; among the 16 reconstructed families of the second (1627) Krmpote migration to Lič (Pavličević 1989) Saric-2008-Bunjevci (medium confidence). 1712 popis: present in Lika regiment parishes (e.g. Kompolje); also Tomljenović variant in Zavalje (Ogulin regiment).

In Desnica II (1684–1749) — extended

wiki/surnames/Vlasi-Uskoplja.title: Vlasi-Uskoplja
wiki/surnames/Vlasi-Uskoplja.content:
Vlasi Uskoplja
Vlach katun from bosanska nahija Uskoplje (1516: 24 dzemats, 248 houses), of older Hercegovinian origin (Nikšić, Banjani). 4 dzemats migrated c. 1528 to area around Plavno, Knin, Kosovo, and the springs of Cetina; significant numbers later joined the uskok migration through Bihać to Žumberak under vojvoda Vuk-Popovic-b???? Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

wiki/surnames/Vlastelica.title: Vlastelica
wiki/surnames/Vlastelica.content:
Vlastelica
Single-cluster attestation: Marko Vlastelica — 1684-02-22 named among the post-uskakanje capi at Vrana (doc. 377). 1684-02-28 the same name appears in the Knin captain Mustaj-beg Firdusović’s letter to Morlacchi sudditi turcheschi who were forced to defect (doc. 380): “Marco Vulastelizza et a Martin Despot et a Rubel et a Bili Vuch et a Blaich et a Piero e Duijam Zalich” — i.e. these are the named leaders the Knin Turks knew by name.

wiki/surnames/Vlasto.title: Vlasto
wiki/surnames/Vlasto.content:
Vlasto
Greek (or Greek-rite) clergy line.
Bearers

pop don Grigorije (Gregorio) Vlasto — 1671-06-21 capelan and parohijski sveštenik of pravoslavnih Morlaka of the Spianata (Sv. Ivan church). 1671-06-25 disputes with the Trećoredci of Sv. Ivan over the colusorne contracts they had signed with the deceased kaluđer Mihail Zarcanin (docs. 193, 194). 1672-11-28 baptizes Bojana Novaković at Sv. Ilija Zadar (doc. 203).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Dimo (Dimitrije) Vlastò — Greek; appointed governor of both Obrovci 1693-01-10, replacing late Cesare Casanova; salary 14 ducats; oversaw salt customs (doc. 260) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Vlatkovic.title: Vlatkovic
wiki/surnames/Vlatkovic.content:
Vlatković (Jurjević-Vlatković)
Catholic Bosnian-Hum noble lineage holding lands in late-medieval western Hercegovina. Augustin-Vlatkovic-b???? (fra) entered Ottoman service c. 1482 with peasant and Vlach subjects, governing vojvodaluk Gornje Primorje, Gorska župa and Ljubuški (later nahije Fragustin, Primorje, Ljubuški) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Augustin-Vlatkovic-b???? — fra, vojvoda in Ottoman service from c. 1482.
D. Vičko Vlatković — Novigrad parohijski paroh, killed 1662-02-13 at Otres (Novigradska godovna knjiga, doc. 119 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Don Luca (Luka) Vlatković — canonico (presumably of Zadar/Nin); age 65 in 1699 (b. ~1634); sworn testimony in Sfakioto’s Grimani-commission protocols re Morlacca (doc. 315) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Vojevic.title: Vojevic
wiki/surnames/Vojevic.content:
Vojević
Bearers in Desnica II

Giacomo Vojević (Jakov Vojević) — serdar of Blato; 10 ducats/month 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Vojic.title: Vojic
wiki/surnames/Vojic.content:
Vojić
