harambaša Gregorio Vojić (Grgur Vojić) — Goranci 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Vojkorsic.title: Vojkorsic
wiki/surnames/Vojkorsic.content:
Vojkorsić
Bearers

Vuko Vojkorsić — harambaša of the Čitluk Morlaks; came over to Venetian devotion with his family ~March 1685; awarded 2 zecchini (doc 54) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Vojnic.title: Vojnic
wiki/surnames/Vojnic.content:
Vojnić (Vojihnić)
Catholic Vlach (Bunjevac) lineage from western Hercegovina — one of the three core Bunjevac katuns of the 1477 defter (with Krmpotic and Sladovic).
Medieval and early-Ottoman attestations

1408 — first mention as Vlasi Vojihnići in a charter of Bosnian king Stjepan Ostoja; subjects of the W. Hum noble line Radivojević-Vlatković Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
1477 — Hercegovina defter, nahija Mostar: džemat of Vukasin-sin-Vojihne-b????-Mostar, 10 houses + 3 unmarried. Wintered/summered with vojvoda Vladimir’s katun across W. Hercegovinian planinas and župas.

Klis sandjak phase
Colonized into the conquered Croatian frontier in the early 16th c. The village Vojnić near Trilj likely a transit toponym. By Hrabak’s evidence, also at Dobropoljci in Bukovica. After the Cyprus-War-1570-1573, Ferhat-beg-Sokolovic-b???? resettled them on his new Tinj vakuf (1573–1574); the area thereafter known as Vojnići or Županovići, after starešine Milos-Zupanovic-b????-Tinj and Filip-Zupanovic-b????-Tinj. 1550: dzemat of knez Mihovil-Vojihnic-b????-Sinj in nahija Sinj Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
17th c. — split between three powers

1605 — 15 Vojnić families joined the Krmpote migration to Lic: Božić, Galešić, Jurjević, Matijević, Pavličić, Petković, Stojčević, Vojnić, Vojnović.
1619 — starešine Miloš Županović and Mate-Vuksic-b????-Tinj negotiated with the senjski kapetan to bring ~1500 Vojnići to Habsburg territory; migration did not happen.
1636 — Forza vizitacija reports župa Županovići: 6 villages (Gorica, Raštane, Prkos, Bubnjane, Lišane Tinjske, Brkljačina Polača), 1550 souls; župnik Stipan-Soric-b????-Gorica.
1647 (Candian War) — most Vojnići crossed to Venetian territory. Knez Filip-Zupanovic-b????-Tinj led part of them to Valtura near Pula.

Possible Bačka connection
Per Sekulić 1986, the Vojnić family of Subotica (ennobled 1741, listed among Subotica graničari 1687) traces origin to Dalmatia — Šarić raises but doesn’t resolve whether they descend from the Tinj/Županović Vojnići Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Bearers in this wiki

Vukasin-sin-Vojihne-b????-Mostar — 1477 katun head
Mihovil-Vojihnic-b????-Sinj — knez (1550)
Milos-Zupanovic-b????-Tinj — starešina (1619)
Filip-Zupanovic-b????-Tinj — knez (1647)
Mate-Vuksic-b????-Tinj — starešina (1619)

wiki/surnames/Vrancic.title: Vrancic
wiki/surnames/Vrancic.content:
Vrančić
Šibenik-zaleđe lineage; merged with Mandušić after Vuk Mandušić’s death in 1648 left no closer male heir than his sister’s son Tadija Vrančić. Style becomes Mandušić alias Vrančić.
Bearers

Tadija Vrančić — see Tadija-Vrancic-b????-Sibenik.
Žorži Mandušić-Vrančić — father of Tadija (doc. 60).

wiki/surnames/Vrsaljko.title: Vrsaljko
wiki/surnames/Vrsaljko.content:
Vrsaljko
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Janko Vrsalj (Gianco Vrsagl) — new settler at Plavno; built strong fence/recinto sheltering 50+ families; appointed harambaša 1694-12-23 (doc. 278) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Vucic.title: Vucic
wiki/surnames/Vucic.content:
Vučić
Patronymic from Vuk (wolf). Distinct from the chunk-2 Vuconie Cvitanović and from any modern Vučić of Serbia.
Bearers

Bili (Bjeli) Vučić — harambaša of Vrana; signatory of the 1684 Vrana petitions (docs 35, 36) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Vucina.title: Vucina
wiki/surnames/Vucina.content:
Vučina
Bearers in Desnica II

Jurašin Vučina — glavar Parčića (headman of Parčić), Krmpote–Parčić church-area dispute 1697 (doc. 301 footnote) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Vukcevic.title: Vukcevic
wiki/surnames/Vukcevic.content:
Vukčević
Bearers

Mileta Vukčević, harambaša — 1648-07-08 4 ducati/month assigned by Foscolo, “comune, pello e barba castagna quadra, occhi uarii, segnato nel ciglio sinistro” (doc. 33). 1648-07-17: “Žegarani uskočeni pod Nin od 200 pješaka izgubili deset” at Ribnik (doc. 39).
Pavle (Paval) Vukčević — 1663-05-08 harambaša guarding the Brusevo pass with men of Žegar, Ervenik and Posedarje (doc. 130). 1666-05-06 elected vice-harambaša of Posedarje by unanimous vote during Stojan Janković’s captivity (doc. 152).
Nikola Vukčević — 1673-05-01 piezzo for Vuko Kovač (doc. 204). 1684-04-07 with Jovan Sinobad and others, victim of Ilija Mitrović’s plundering (doc. 391).
Vuk Vukčević — 1679-05-16 protected by mandate from his son’s kidnappers (doc. 247): “ne per se ne per interposte persone ardiscano offender, molestar, o inquietar…” Vule (a son of Dragosav Capelletto Budin) and Bogoie his nephew are warned off Radojica Garković’s house — Vukčević / Garković feud spillover.
Vukadin Vukčević — 1679 son of Dragosav (doc. 247).
Bogoje Vukčević — 1679 nephew of Dragosav (doc. 247).
Guozden Vuccevich — 1684-04-07 also among the Sinobad case complainants (doc. 391).
Simon Vuccevich — 1684-04-07 ditto (doc. 391).

Notes

The Vukčevići of Budin are documented in 1684 in feud (krvarina) with the Mitrovići; Polo Michiel asked to mediate (doc 15, Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II).
Per Desnica’s 1951 editorial footnote (to doc 115), the Vukčević surname is still present in Žegar today (1951). Together with Zelić, Radmilović, and Nanić, the families “came in 1648 with the Jankovićs to Budim near Posedarje and during the Morean War many returned to Lika; Budim is today (1951) ruins”. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

wiki/surnames/Vukdrasinovic.content:
Vukdrašinović

wiki/surnames/Vukelic.title: Vukelic
wiki/surnames/Vukelic.content:

wiki/surnames/Vukmirovic.title: Vukmirovic
wiki/surnames/Vukmirovic.content:
Vukmirović

wiki/surnames/Vukobratovic.title: Vukobratovic
wiki/surnames/Vukobratovic.content:
Vukobratović
Single attestation: harambaša Ivanko (Ivanco) Vukobratović barjaktar (alfier) serdara Ilije Smiljanovića — 1654-01-12, “di statura comune, mostacchi pel castagno, barba rasa, d’ anni trentadue in circa” (b. ~1622) — pay 4 ducati/month assigned by Dolfin (doc. 79).

wiki/surnames/Vukosalkic.title: Vukosalkic
wiki/surnames/Vukosalkic.content:
Vukosalkić

wiki/surnames/Vukovic.title: Vukovic
wiki/surnames/Vukovic.content:
Vuković

wiki/surnames/Zapic.title: Zapic
wiki/surnames/Zapic.content:
Žapić
Bearers

wiki/surnames/Zarcanin.title: Zarcanin
wiki/surnames/Zarcanin.content:
Žarčanin
Single attestation: kaluđer Mihail Zarcanin — d. before 1671. The Trećoredci’s insussistenti contracts attributed to him for the Sv. Ivan church repudiated by his successor Grigorije Vlasto (doc. 194).

wiki/surnames/Zdunic.title: Zdunic
wiki/surnames/Zdunic.content:
Zdunić
Bunjevac priest-family surname in Lika at the time of the 1712 popis Saric-2008-Bunjevci:

Damjan-Zdunic-b????-Lovinac — župnik Lovinca; the pop Zduna of folk tradition.
Simun-Zdunic-b????-Smiljan — župnik Smiljana.

wiki/surnames/Zelic.title: Zelic
wiki/surnames/Zelic.content:
Zelić
Bukovica surname attested in Žegar.
Notes

Per Desnica’s 1951 editorial footnote (to doc 115), the Zelić surname is still present in Žegar today (1951). Together with Radmilović, Vukčević, and Nanić, the families “came in 1648 with the Jankovićs to Budim near Posedarje and during the Morean War many returned to Lika; Budim is today (1951) ruins”. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

In Desnica II (1684–1749) — bearers

Nikola Zelić (Nicola Zelich) da Žegar — brother-in-law (cognato) of late kavalier Zaviša Mitrović; appointed vice-serdar of Upper Kotari 1731-12-29 by Sebastian Vendramin to assist the young serdar Kirijak Dedić-Janković; called “zio” (uncle) of Kirijak (doc. 384) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Zen.title: Zen
wiki/surnames/Zen.content:
Zen
Venetian patrician house.
Bearers

Girolamo Zen — procurator; signatory of doc 22 (1684) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Antonio Zeno — Provveditor General della cavalleria 1686–1687; reports on Sinj siege (doc 133, doc 134) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
provveditor estraordinario Zen — based at Cattaro, sends Korponež with galeotta to Pastrovići March 1686 (doc 131) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Zepina.title: Zepina
wiki/surnames/Zepina.content:
Žepina
Bearers

Kojadin Žepina — Morlak alfiere from Zadar territory; lost his arm at Plavno 1684 attacking Durakbegović’s tower; awarded by ducal in doc. 2 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Zigo.title: Zigo
wiki/surnames/Zigo.content:
Žigo
Bearers in Desnica II

harambaša Vido Žigo (Vid Žigo) — Brochno 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Zinovic.title: Zinovic
wiki/surnames/Zinovic.content:
Žinović
Bearers

Žinović (Xinovich) — capo of the Šibenik-Skradin territory Morlachs; with Goreta and Palikuća during the November 1686 Bribir defeat (doc 155) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Zirovac.title: Zirovac
wiki/surnames/Zirovac.content:
Zirovac
Vicko-Zirovac-b????-Kistanje led a Vlach dzemat (likely orthodox) on the former Zečevo nahija lands by 1550 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Vicko-Zirovac-b????-Kistanje — vojvoda i knez (1550)

wiki/surnames/Zoric.title: Zoric
wiki/surnames/Zoric.content:
Zorić
Bjelaj-area capi family of the 1692 mass migration.
Bearers in Desnica II

Todoro Zorić (Todor Zorich) — capo of Bjelaj province with Đurić and Pirić; led ~5000 souls to Venetian devotion 1692; settled in Plavno area Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs. 251, 252).

wiki/surnames/Zrinski.title: Zrinski
wiki/surnames/Zrinski.content:
Zrinski
Croatian magnatial house. Nikola-Zrinski-b???? settled 25 Mušković Vlach families on his ribničko vlastelinstvo at Prilisce and Rosopajnik (Vukova Gorica) in 1544, granting them hereditary libertini status (deed 25 June 1544) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Nikola-Zrinski-b???? — magnate (1544)

wiki/surnames/Zucovic.title: Zucovic
wiki/surnames/Zucovic.content:
Zucović
Bearers in Desnica II

Zorzi Zucović (Đorđe Žuković/Zucović) — serdar; 10 ducats/month 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Zuljevic.title: Zuljevic
wiki/surnames/Zuljevic.content:
Žuljević
Bearers

don Pavao (Pava) Žuljević — redovnik (priest) from the Poljica province; volunteered to enter slavery at Sinj as a hostage substitute for vojvoda Ivan Marušić in the cell of Šain-aga Mandić, while Marušić travelled to discuss his ransom with the generale Valier (doc 110, undated, Marušić’s Bosnian-Cyrillic letter to Stipan Garković) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/Zupanovic.title: Zupanovic
wiki/surnames/Zupanovic.content:
Županović (Župan)
Vojnić starešina family — gives name to the “Županovići” subregion around Tinj Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. The Catholic-Vlach population of this župa was pastorally tended by don Stjepan Sorić in 1636 Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Bearers (Desnica)

harambaša Bose (Bože) Županović — 1647-08-31 capitan in Foscolo’s command (doc. 16); 1652-09-24 holds the Turk Rustem-beg as his slave purchased from Janko Mitrović after the Grahovo battle (doc. 64); 1653-01-16 governator Bose Zuppanovich co-signs the proxy authorising Smiljanić to plead in Venice (doc. 70). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Jadre Zuppanović (Župan) — from Gorica; killed by Ilija Janković in 1692 (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Tomica Župan (Tomiza Zupan) — Obrovac inhabitant 1696 (doc. 284) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

wiki/surnames/del-Borro.title: del-Borro
wiki/surnames/del-Borro.content:
del Borro
Tuscan-Italian marchesi in Venetian military service.
Bearers

Nicolò del Borro — marchese, sergente maggior battaglia Dalmatia 1684–85 (docs 33, 60–61); later sargente generale di battaglia (doc 10388) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
